items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: If you laid the Himalayas across central India, Delhi could lose its monsoon. And freeze.
Why? India's weather runs on one wall.
Right now, it's a twenty-four hundred kilometre wall along India's top edge.
Every summer, monsoon winds slam into it, rise, and dump their rain on the south side.
Behind the wall, almost nothing gets through. Leh gets about a hundred millimetres of rain a year.
So what happens if we drag the wall south?
Line it up on the Tropic of Cancer, right across the middle of India.
Everest would now stand about five hundred kilometres south... a short drive from Dhanbad.
The monsoon hits the wall halfway up the country. The south gets soaked.
But Delhi is now behind it. In the rain shadow.
[stunned, offended, posh old city, slow] Wait. I'm the new Ladakh?
And winter gets worse. Today, the Himalayas block icy winds from Central Asia.
Move it, and those winds blow straight into the plains.
[shivering, deadpan, sarcastic] Less rain. More cold. Great deal.
So India's weather isn't decided by where India sits. It's decided by where its wall stands.
Here's the twist. The wall isn't moving south. India is moving north, into it... about five centimetres a year.
[huge, slow, deep, smug and calm giant mountain] Relax, Delhi. You're coming to me.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
